newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gaddum - economy suggests current rates correct.
newsitem.headline: Gaddum - economy suggests current rates correct.

text.p: Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said on Wednesday current economic conditions and M3 money supply data indicated that present interest rate levels were correct.
Gaddum, speaking ahead of the Bundesbank's twice-monthly council meeting on Thursday, told reporters the German central bank wanted to keep rates at their current levels for as long as possible.
"The economic situation and the development of money supply support the fact that the current level of interest rates is appropriate," Gaddum said.
He said the Bundesbank would review the situation with rates once new economic data was available.
On the subject of the securities repurchase rate, now fixed at three percent, Gaddum said the conditions for sticking with a fixed-rate tender remained valid.
Gaddum also said the current exchange rate between the mark and the dollar was no cause for concern.
Gaddum's attitude on rates reinforces earlier comments by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing, who said there was no reason to expect interest rates to be lowered.
